item.title: Roe 8 Corridor Rehabilitation: 200,000 plants and 97 species return; ecosystem only 30% restored
item.description: Almost ten years post the controversial Roe 8 highway initiative, Western Australia is witnessing a promising wave of ecological recovery. Recent studies have reported a remarkable resurgence of local wildlife and native plant life. Rehabilitation efforts, which have culminated in planting over 280,000 seedlings, are welcoming back species such as Carnaby’s black cockatoos. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Drought shifts more plant root cells into newly discovered environmental response mode
item.description: Scientists have discovered a hidden layer of identity in plant root cells: an "environmental mode" that switches on in some cells and becomes more common when water is scarce. The study, led by Dr. Marina Oliva and professor Ryan Lister, from the ARC Center of Excellence in Plants for Space and The University of Western Australia's School of Molecular Sciences, examined how plant cells responded to drought conditions. The work is published in Nature Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Curtain-like plasma structures explain solar jets' apparent spinning in simulations
item.description: An international team of scientists from the University of Sheffield and the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, led by a postdoctoral research fellow from the University of Newcastle, Australia, has discovered that solar jets called spicules, which are 6–8 Mm long, take the form of warped, denser plasma sheets like pleated drapery. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Drone measurements reveal rapid early growth in eastern Australian humpback whales
item.description: Eastern Australian humpback whales reach nearly their full adult size quickly, a new Griffith University–led study has found, as shown by the first contemporary growth curves for this recovering whale population. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The great moth revival: how bogongs have bounced back
item.description: This animated map shows the insect’s population exploding in Australia’s eastern states, with the endangered species coming back from the brink If you live anywhere on the eastern side of Australia, you’ve probably noticed that bogong moths are back in a big way . While we don’t yet have figures from ecologist-led surveys to compare with previous years, there is a wealth of data on the great moth revival being generated by citizen scientists across the eastern states. item.title: ‘Jane Austen is for everyone’: novelist Diana Reid on adapting Sense and Sensibility – and surprising Brits with her accent
item.description: The Australian author of Love and Virtue says her nationality didn’t give her pause when she wrote the script, but Ang Lee’s ‘perfect’ 1995 film did The summer Diana Reid spent writing her film adaptation of Sense and Sensibility , she found herself having some oddly formal conversations down at the pub. The Australian author used only about 25 lines from Jane Austen’s first published novel for her screenplay, inventing most of the dialogue herself. To be able to mimic that very distinctive voice, Reid had to dive headfirst into studying Austen’s rhythm and sentence structure. “I got so… Fuente: The Guardian - Culture.

item.description: Assessment finds global heating is endangering 96% of coral reefs across 80 countries – a figure scientists say should serve as a ‘wake-up call’ Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here Almost every shallow-water coral reef on the planet, including Australia’s Great Barrier Reef, faces a high risk of ecosystem collapse before 2075 because of global heating, according to an assessment by United Nations nature advisers. About 24% of the planet’s reefs across more than 80 countries are already critically endangered, the assessment said, but when the… Publicado también por: The Guardian - Environment. item.title: Shark trapped in South Korean city won't return to sea
item.description: Although "Bukangi" has become a mascot for the city of Busan, everyone agrees the dusky shark should go back to the open sea. But getting her to leave is proving difficult. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: La diputada australiana atropellada pierde sus piernas y la familia del presunto agresor se declara amiga de la víctima desde hace 20 años
item.description: Helen Haines , la diputada australiana que fue atropellada deliberadamente este lunes, ha perdido sus dos piernas. Tras ser trasladada de urgencia al Hospital Alfred de Melbourne (Australia) , los cirujanos han tenido que amputarle los dos miembros inferiores para salvar su vida y ahora su estado es estable, según ha afirmado su esposo, Phil Haines. El gran giro de este caso ha venido por parte de la familia del presunto agresor , quien ha declarado que lo ocurrido fue «devastador» para ellos , puesto que llevaban siendo amigos desde hace 20 años, según ha adelantado 'The Guardian'.
